text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000568 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, including low-complexity patients, but no 99215 charts were returned to confirm or refute support.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not explained by panel acuity alone: this provider's 99215 share runs above the all-provider share in every condition-count tier, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine-looking encounters such as follow-up (Z09) on C0296869 and C0297207, upper respiratory infection on C0297375 and C0298230, and UTI on C0297316, which is a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, the sampled high-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0297903 and C0297571) involve patients with four or five chronic conditions where a high level is plausible, and the modest peer z-score shows this provider is not a dramatic outlier on unadjusted rates. The documentation is too thin to judge: only 14 charts came back, all billed 99213 or 99214 and all supported, with none at 99215, and the single data-reviewed note with no matching lab line is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request records for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, starting with the Z09, J06.9 and N39.0 visits, to check whether the documented MDM and time support level 5."}
